propositions: A one-time backfill script must measure cyclomatic complexity (via lizard) and clone count (via jscpd) at sampled historical commits and write snapshots with those metrics to the going-forward store.
Each backfilled snapshot must be timestamped with the commit's committer date (git show -s --format=%cI), not the wall-clock backfill-run time, so trends remain meaningful.
The measure_tree() function shells to lizard and jscpd tools, parsing complexity as summed cyclomatic complexity across all functions and clone_count from jscpd-report.json statistics.total.clones.
If either tool is absent or errors on a commit, measure_tree() returns None and that commit is skipped with logging; the backfill continues non-fatally.
Every written snapshot is tagged with source="snapshot" and confidence="high" and written through the same snapshot.py writer as the going-forward path.
The script supports a configurable sampling cadence (default monthly) as a command-line argument.
